I have enough strong evidence. Let me now synthesize the research note.

# Lens 1B.1 Research Note — Vladimir Putin, 2023

**Question 1B.1:** Did the ruler seek to reduce nuclear or other existential risk, rather than increase prestige, leverage, or personal power through escalation?

**Summary of evidence direction:** The evidence strongly indicates Putin acted to *increase* nuclear risk for leverage/prestige in 2023, not to reduce it. Two major escalatory actions: (1) suspending Russia's participation in New START (Feb 21, 2023), eliminating the last bilateral arms-control inspection regime; (2) announcing and proceeding with deployment of tactical nuclear weapons to Belarus (announced March 25, signed May 25, facilities ready July 7–8, 2023). No countervailing de-escalation, risk-reduction, or restraint measures were documented in 2023.

---

## Claim-level evidence items

### Item 1 — Russia suspends New START participation
- **Title:** "Putin: Russia suspends participation in last remaining nuclear treaty with US"
- **Publisher:** Reuters
- **Date:** 2023-02-21
- **URL:** https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/putin-russia-suspends-participation-last-remaining-nuclear-treaty-with-us-2023-02-21/
- **Claim summary:** On 21 February 2023, President Vladimir Putin announced Russia was suspending its participation in the New START treaty — the last remaining US-Russia strategic nuclear arms-control agreement limiting deployed strategic warheads and delivery systems. This ended on-site inspections and data exchanges that had been a key transparency mechanism.
- **Question IDs:** 1B.1 (primary — increased opacity and arms-control rollback); also relevant to broader nuclear posture/leadership evaluation.

### Item 2 — US State Department confirmation of suspension
- **Title:** "2023 Report to Congress on Implementation of the New START Treaty"
- **Publisher:** US Department of State, Bureau of Arms Control, Deterrence, and Stability
- **Date:** 2024-01-31 (covering 2023 events)
- **URL:** https://www.state.gov/bureau-of-arms-control-deterrence-and-stability/releases/2024/01/2023-report-to-congress-on-implementation-of-the-new-start-treaty
- **Claim summary:** Official US government report documenting that "On February 21, 2023, President Putin announced that Russia would suspend its participation in the New START Treaty," confirming the date, actor, and significance as the last bilateral strategic-arms accord.
- **Question IDs:** 1B.1.

### Item 3 — Analysis: suspension increases nuclear risks
- **Title:** "Russia Suspends New START and Increases Nuclear Risks"
- **Publisher:** Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
- **Date:** 2023-02-23
- **URL:** https://www.csis.org/analysis/russia-suspends-new-start-and-increases-nuclear-risks
- **Claim summary:** CSIS analysis explicitly frames the suspension as increasing nuclear risks by eliminating one of the few remaining forums for US-Russia nuclear dialogue and verification, and weakening the bilateral arms-control architecture.
- **Question IDs:** 1B.1.

### Item 4 — Putin announces tactical nuclear weapons deployment to Belarus
- **Title:** "Putin says Russia will station nuclear weapons in Belarus"
- **Publisher:** BBC News
- **Date:** 2023-03-26
- **URL:** https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-65077687
- **Claim summary:** Putin announced on 25 March 2023 that Russia would station tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus. Putin framed the move as not violating nuclear non-proliferation commitments (Russia would retain control), but it was widely read as a warning to the West over Ukraine military aid.
- **Question IDs:** 1B.1 (primary — geographic proliferation of nuclear weapons on a neighbor's territory, increasing forward-deployed posture and signaling leverage).

### Item 5 — Russia and Belarus sign deployment document
- **Title:** "Russia and Belarus Sign Document on Tactical Nuclear Weapon Deployment"
- **Publisher:** The Moscow Times
- **Date:** 2023-05-25
- **URL:** https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2023/05/25/russia-and-belarus-sign-document-on-tactical-nuclear-weapon-deployment-a81280
- **Claim summary:** On 25 May 2023, the Russian and Belarusian defense ministers signed the formal document operationalizing the deployment of Russian tactical nuclear weapons on Belarusian territory — moving from announcement to binding bilateral agreement.
- **Question IDs:** 1B.1.

### Item 6 — Putin confirms deployment to begin July 2023
- **Title:** "Putin says tactical nuclear weapons to be deployed in Belarus in July"
- **Publisher:** Reuters
- **Date:** 2023-06-09
- **URL:** https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-belarus-july-putin-says-2023-06-09/
- **Claim summary:** Putin told reporters on 9 June 2023 that Russia would begin deploying tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus once storage facilities were ready on 7–8 July 2023 — confirming operational execution of the deployment within 2023.
- **Question IDs:** 1B.1.

### Item 7 — Wikipedia compilation of nuclear-risk events (used as cross-reference index, not primary evidence)
- **Title:** "Nuclear risk during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)"
- **Publisher:** Wikipedia
- **Date:** Continuously updated
- **URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_risk_during_the_Russo-Ukrainian_war_(2022%E2%80%93present)
- **Claim summary:** Cross-reference summarizing the March 2023 Belarus deployment announcement and the stationing of tactical nuclear weapons via Iskander short-range ballistic missiles and Su-25 gravity bombs. Useful as an indexed timeline, but for 1B.1 the primary Reuters/BBC/State Department sources above carry the load.
- **Question IDs:** 1B.1 (corroborative).

---

## Evidence direction

- **Against risk reduction (escalation / leverage behavior):** Items 1, 2, 3 (New START suspension); Items 4, 5, 6 (Belarus tactical nuclear deployment, March–July 2023).
- **In favor of risk reduction:** No documented 2023 Putin action was identified that reduced nuclear or other existential risk. On the contrary, analysis (Item 3) and contemporaneous reporting frame his actions as risk-increasing and leverage-seeking.

## Search gap notes

- No primary Kremlin speech transcript was retrieved in this round; the Reuters/BBC quotes are the available primary quotations.
- The Congressional Research Service IF12672 ("In February 2023, President Putin noted the possibility of Russian nuclear tests if the United States were to engage in such testing") was indexed but not opened in this 6-call budget; it is consistent with — and would reinforce — the escalation direction documented above.
- No 2023 evidence of a Russian de-escalation initiative, risk-reduction dialogue offer, or restraint on nuclear signaling was found within the call budget; the absence appears genuine rather than a search gap, given saturation on New START and Belarus.
